description: Copy rules for Carousel Studio (CONTRACT 7.4). Word lists read by the Python engine (_cs.qa, _cs.lint) and the browser engine (CS.qa) with identical results. Entries are written without diacritics or tatweel because matching strips both from the text first. Arabic entries apply to every dialect unless 'dialects' narrows them; English entries are marked ['en'].

aiWords.description: Words and phrases that make copy read as machine-written (Arabic and English). C8.ai-words, FIX; voice_check.py flags them too.

note.ar: فعل أمر شائع في نصوص الذكاء الاصطناعي (ارتق بمحتواك).

stockOpeners.description: Dead openers for a cover, a first caption line or a first slide sentence. C8.stock-opener, FIX. Dialect-specific entries only fire in that dialect.

hypeWords.description: Empty-slot hype: intensity with no specific fact behind it. C8.hype, FIX. Single adjectives are NOTE-level because they can be legitimate next to a real fact.

abstractWords.description: Abstract nouns that say nothing a reader can picture. C8.abstract, NOTE; the hook score takes 5 points off per word. Replace with a concrete noun, a named tool, a number or a time.

fearWords.description: Fear and loss vocabulary. One negative word is fine (costly-mistake hooks use one); fear STACKING means several distinct entries in the same hook, slide or caption (SEN1.fear-stacking, threshold in qa-rules.json; hook gate HG5).

conspiracy.description: Conspiracy and suppression framing: someone is hiding the truth from you. SEN1, BLOCK.

entries.text: ما لا يريدك أحد أن تعرفه
they don't want you to know
they don’t want you to know

overclaim.description: Guarantees, effortless-result promises and unprovable absolutes. Describe what the thing does, not what will happen to the reader. Superlatives like 'best' are NOT listed: they are normal in 'best 5 tools' posts.

note.ar: ادعاء قد يكون صحيحا؛ تأكد من أن المصدر أو المستخدم يؤكده.
note.en: May be true; confirm the user or a source backs it.

commentBait.description: Engagement bait: asks for a like, a tag, an emoji or an arbitrary word with nothing delivered in return. C4.bait, BLOCK. A keyword the reader types to RECEIVE a real asset is not listed here; that case is governed by C4.keyword-asset (instant delivery).

introPhrases.description: Intro, agenda and bio phrases. Slide 2 is a second cover that pays off at once, so any of these there is a C3.intro BLOCK (overridable).

stiffMsa.description: Chancellery and letter-writing Arabic that no creator speaks. C8.stiff-msa, FIX. 'White' MSA keeps the grammar but drops these formulas.

translationese.description: Arabic words arranged in English order. The test is the sentence, not the word: restructure rather than swap. C8.translationese, FIX (NOTE where the phrase is often legitimate).

note.ar: قم بـ + مصدر ترجمة حرفية؛ استعمل الفعل مباشرة.
note.en: 'قم بـ' + noun is a calque of 'do the X-ing'; use the verb itself.

entries.suggest: ابدأ بالفعل مباشرة: اضغط، افتح، أضف، حمّل

note.ar: المبني للمجهول المترجم يخفي الفاعل؛ سمّه.
note.en: Calqued passive hides the doer; name it.

entries.suggest: سمّ الفاعل: يصلك، تحصل على، نرسل
استعمل الفعل نفسه بدل يقوم بـ + مصدر

note.ar: ترجمة حرفية للفعل الإنجليزي؛ قل ما سيفعله القارئ فعلا (افتح، جرّب، حمّل).
note.en: Calque of 'get'; say what the reader actually does.

note.ar: سليمة بمعنى «سابقا»، وترجمة حرفية حين تدل على الفاعل (تم تصميمه من قبل).
note.en: Fine as 'before'; a calque when it marks the agent of a passive.

bindLabels.description: Nouns that name a numbered thing (step 3, tip 5). When one is followed by a number the pair is joined with U+00A0 so it never splits across lines. Matching uses proclitics, so 'الخطوة' and 'للخطوة' are covered by 'خطوة'.

numberWords.description: Spelled-out numbers. A cover uses digits, so a hit inside cover text is C1.number-words (FIX); keep the words for speech. 'value' is the digit to use instead.
